Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the administration of Regional Government.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of trafficking victims from health disorders suffered.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return trafficking victims from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter referred to as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and manners of social life of the Hindu community passed down from generation to generation in the bonds of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 5

(1) The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;

b. monitoring, strengthening of victims of violence; c. capacity building of apparatus and other stakeholders.

Article 11

(1) The Minimum Service Standards as referred to in Article 10 have performance indicators including:

a. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive complaint handling by trained officers in the integrated service unit;
b. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive health services by trained health personnel at Community Health Centers and Hospitals:
c. coverage of social rehabilitation services provided by trained social rehabilitation officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
d. coverage of spiritual guidance services provided by trained spiritual guidance officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
e. coverage of law enforcement from the investigation level to court decisions on cases of violence against women and children;
f. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive legal aid services;
g. coverage of repatriation services for women and child victims of violence; and
h. coverage of social reintegration services for women and child victims of violence.
(2) The determination of performance indicators for the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes the minimum target that must be achieved by the integrated service unit in stages.

Article 13

(1) The Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence in the region.

Article 3

The objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence are:

a. to protect women and children victims of violence; b. to provide services to women and children victims of violence; and
c. empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Tabanan Regency.

NUMBER 11 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 14

(1) Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of related Regional Apparatus Work Units on a regular basis.

(2) Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence for the current year.

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and child victims of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are:

a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; and
c. legal certainty.

Article 15

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII

SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSES

Article 16

(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing reports on the implementation of the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence and submitting them to the Governor with copies submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.

(2) Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted annually.

(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures and forms of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 18

The Regent conducts development and supervision of the implementation of the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the region.

Article 16

Sufficiently clear

Article 20

Sufficiently clear

Article 12

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to establish Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses or other designations.

(2) Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses as referred to in paragraph (1) guarantee the implementation of health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration.

(3) For the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the regional government may utilize social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

CHAPTER XIII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 5

(1) The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;

b. monitoring, strengthening of victims of violence; c. capacity building of apparatus and other stakeholders.

Article 3

The objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence are:

a. to protect women and children victims of violence; b. to provide services to women and children victims of violence; and
c. empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

Article 11

(1) The Minimum Service Standards as referred to in Article 10 have performance indicators including:

a. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive complaint handling by trained officers in the integrated service unit;
b. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive health services by trained health personnel at Community Health Centers and Hospitals:
c. coverage of social rehabilitation services provided by trained social rehabilitation officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
d. coverage of spiritual guidance services provided by trained spiritual guidance officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
e. coverage of law enforcement from the investigation level to court decisions on cases of violence against women and children;
f. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive legal aid services;
g. coverage of repatriation services for women and child victims of violence; and
h. coverage of social reintegration services for women and child victims of violence.

Article 13

(1) The Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence in the region.

Article 14

(1) Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of related Regional Apparatus Work Units on a regular basis.

(2) Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence for the current year.

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and child victims of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tabanan Regency.

3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.

5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of trafficking victims from health disorders suffered.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return trafficking victims from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter referred to as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and manners of social life of the Hindu community passed down from generation to generation in the bonds of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the administration of Regional Government.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of trafficking victims from health disorders suffered.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return trafficking victims from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter referred to as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and manners of social life of the Hindu community passed down from generation to generation in the bonds of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 14

(1) Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of related Regional Apparatus Work Units on a regular basis.

(2) Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence for the current year.

Article 13

(1) The Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence in the region.

Article 5

(1) The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;

b. monitoring, strengthening of victims of violence; c. capacity building of apparatus and other stakeholders.

Article 3

The objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence are:

a. to protect women and children victims of violence; b. to provide services to women and children victims of violence; and
c. empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are:

a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; and
c. legal certainty.

Article 16

(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing reports on the implementation of the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence and submitting them to the Governor with copies submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.

(2) Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted annually.

(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures and forms of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 11

(1) The Minimum Service Standards as referred to in Article 10 have performance indicators including:

a. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive complaint handling by trained officers in the integrated service unit;
b. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive health services by trained health personnel at Community Health Centers and Hospitals:
c. coverage of social rehabilitation services provided by trained social rehabilitation officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
d. coverage of spiritual guidance services provided by trained spiritual guidance officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
e. coverage of law enforcement from the investigation level to court decisions on cases of violence against women and children;
f. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive legal aid services;
g. coverage of repatriation services for women and child victims of violence; and
h. coverage of social reintegration services for women and child victims of violence.
(2) The determination of performance indicators for the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes the minimum target that must be achieved by the integrated service unit in stages.

Article 15

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and child victims of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

Article 18

The Regent conducts development and supervision of the implementation of the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the region.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 12

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to establish Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses or other designations.

(2) Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses as referred to in paragraph (1) guarantee the implementation of health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration.

(3) For the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the regional government may utilize social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

Article 18

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and child victims of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are:

a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; and
c. legal certainty.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 12

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to establish Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses or other designations.

(2) Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses as referred to in paragraph (1) guarantee the implementation of health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration.

(3) For the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the regional government may utilize social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

Article 15

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 11

(1) The Minimum Service Standards as referred to in Article 10 have performance indicators including:

a. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive complaint handling by trained officers in the integrated service unit;
b. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive health services by trained health personnel at Community Health Centers and Hospitals:
c. coverage of social rehabilitation services provided by trained social rehabilitation officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
d. coverage of spiritual guidance services provided by trained spiritual guidance officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
e. coverage of law enforcement from the investigation level to court decisions on cases of violence against women and children;
f. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive legal aid services;
g. coverage of repatriation services for women and child victims of violence; and
h. coverage of social reintegration services for women and child victims of violence.
(2) The determination of performance indicators for the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes the minimum target that must be achieved by the integrated service unit in stages.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the administration of Regional Government.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of trafficking victims from health disorders suffered.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return trafficking victims from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter referred to as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and manners of social life of the Hindu community passed down from generation to generation in the bonds of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 14

(1) Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of related Regional Apparatus Work Units on a regular basis.

(2) Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence for the current year.

Article 5

(1) The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;

b. monitoring, strengthening of victims of violence; c. capacity building of apparatus and other stakeholders.

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Tabanan Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

Article 3

The objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence are:

a. to protect women and children victims of violence; b. to provide services to women and children victims of violence; and
c. empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 5

(1) The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;

b. monitoring, strengthening of victims of violence; c. capacity building of apparatus and other stakeholders.

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are:

a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; and
c. legal certainty.

Article 13

(1) The Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence in the region.

Article 11

(1) The Minimum Service Standards as referred to in Article 10 have performance indicators including:

a. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive complaint handling by trained officers in the integrated service unit;
b. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive health services by trained health personnel at Community Health Centers and Hospitals:
c. coverage of social rehabilitation services provided by trained social rehabilitation officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
d. coverage of spiritual guidance services provided by trained spiritual guidance officers for women and child victims of violence in the integrated service unit:
e. coverage of law enforcement from the investigation level to court decisions on cases of violence against women and children;
f. coverage of women and child victims of violence who receive legal aid services;
g. coverage of repatriation services for women and child victims of violence; and
h. coverage of social reintegration services for women and child victims of violence.
(2) The determination of performance indicators for the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes the minimum target that must be achieved by the integrated service unit in stages.

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and child victims of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

Article 14

(1) Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of related Regional Apparatus Work Units on a regular basis.

(2) Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence for the current year.

Article 15

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 16

(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing reports on the implementation of the Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence and submitting them to the Governor with copies submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.

(2) Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted annually.

(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures and forms of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the administration of Regional Government.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of trafficking victims from health disorders suffered.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return trafficking victims from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter referred to as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and manners of social life of the Hindu community passed down from generation to generation in the bonds of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.

20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and manners of social life of the Hindu community passed down from generation to generation in the bonds of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the administration of Regional Government.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman or child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of trafficking victims from health disorders suffered.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return trafficking victims from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter referred to as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and manners of social life of the Hindu community passed down from generation to generation in the bonds of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and child victims of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is a form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore minimum services for victims of violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to be free from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.
